Mechanism (read from the committed diff of 001a791 when this record was written): a new Windows-only src/winfile.rs calls GetFileType on the open handle. read_bounded (shared by profile show and tui) refuses anything that is not FILE_TYPE_DISK with exit 2 USAGE_ERROR before any metadata query or read; the Windows agent connect refuses anything that is not FILE_TYPE_PIPE before the request frame is written. New direct dependency windows-sys =0.61.2 (already in the lock transitively); a second query-only unsafe FFI call under deny(unsafe_code). The causal claim that std is_file() is true for pipe handles, so the read blocked, is the fix round's inference from std semantics and the red/green tests, not traced.

Because the check runs after the handle is opened, Rust still connects to a named pipe given as --file once before refusing (pipe_connects 1, final count, in both the profile and tui rows); --socket opens a regular file read/write before refusing it, with content and mtime shown unchanged. Recorded, not gated under section 9.6.

limitations: Batch-file script path (argv[0]): the independent reviewer found that Rust std puts the batch file's own path into the cmd.exe /c line without the percent-escaping it applies to the arguments, so a %NAME% in the path is expanded by cmd.exe. Observed: with an attacker-controlled variable and a directory named after it a second command ran (INJECTED); <dir>\os%OS%y\fwd.bat ran a different batch file while the intended one never ran. A direct CreateProcessW of the same path without heimdall-proto does the same, so the root cause is cmd.exe. The orchestrator ruled on 2026-10-10 (docs/g02/slice-contract.md section 9.7, uncommitted in the working tree when this record was written): section 9.6 covers argv[1..]; the script path is not gated for G02 because plain exec on Windows behaves the same and plain-exec equivalence is the reference; the production launcher must refuse a batch target whose path contains % (or another character cmd.exe interprets) or not start batch files through cmd.exe, tested natively (M01 input; among the rulings the owner can overrule, ADR-0002 section 10 D3). This record's pass does not mean the script-path exposure is absent in Rust.

Trailing-dot batch names: for fwd.bat., fwd.cmd. and 'fwd.bat. . .' std detects the batch file but passes the un-normalized name to cmd.exe, which reports 'not recognized'; run exits 1 (CHILD_EXITED, launched) instead of running the file or refusing with 127. No injection. Pre-existing std behaviour outside the fix's diff; the reviewer's 9 trailing-dot probe FAILs. No ruling found in the contract; recorded as an M01 input by the reviewer.

Reviewer probe totals: 129 probes, {"FAIL": 12, "INFO": 5, "PASS": 112}. All 12 FAIL probes are in the batch section (9 trailing-dot names, 3 percent-in-script-path); profile, socket and agentpipe sections have 0 FAIL. The reviewer classed the batch items as minor, pre-existing and outside the fix round's diff.

Opening a pipe given as profile show or tui --file connects to the pipe server before GetFileType rejects it (the reviewer's separate-process server logged 2 connects for its 2 opens, no bytes read or written). Section 5 says tui makes no agent contact, and --file \\.\pipe\openssh-ssh-agent would make one connection to a real agent; a path-prefix pre-check cannot cover every pipe alias. M01 should decide whether a connection without traffic counts as contact. A device whose open has side effects (for example a COM port) given as --socket would still be opened briefly.

Build reproducibility: the independent reviewer's clean-copy rebuild reproduced all four dist artifacts and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES byte for byte (sha256 and cmp), including windows-x64 ba80f914a225fd6dcd22767bfcf1b0ded48489ed88081538641a39013fedadac. The fix round's own artifacts disagree on the topic: prototypes/rust/REPORT.md section 6 (Known defects) says the windows-x64 digest is not reproducible between identical builds, while its section 13 (round 2) records a /Brepro fix with a repro-other-checkout step; and build/compare.txt shows a rebuild of unchanged HEAD source (windows-x64 a6d24fe7..., 841728 bytes) differing from the committed round-3c artifact dde9662f... at the same size, and Linux rebuilds of unchanged source no longer matching the committed bytes (environmental drift, not investigated). So the baseline exe dde9662f could not be rebuilt from its source in the fix round, while the post-fix exe ba80f914 was rebuilt once, by the reviewer, with an equal digest. Reproducibility of the Windows digest is not established by this record.

The rebuilt linux-x64 artifact (7b1b3fcf) did not get a fresh native harness run (the X1 linux-x64 139/139 applies to the round-3c bytes); darwin-arm64 and linux-arm64 were run (139/139 each, fix round and reviewer).
